From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantization tradeoffs and model-fit — post-call recap

Alex/Priya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Summary:
- Primary goal: replace FinWave's current on-prem LLM endpoint with a cost-effective, low-latency inference path that preserves answer quality for customer support use cases.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for up to 200 concurrent requests (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Quality bar: <= 5% regression on top-1 intent/answer accuracy vs current baseline (evaluation set provided).
- Desired throughput: initial ramp to 200 rps, peak ~500 rps (batching allowed for throughput windows).

What we agreed to provide next (by EOD Thu):
1) Recommended model family/size candidates for FinWave (tradeoffs on quality vs throughput).
2) AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 trade-study summary with measured token throughput and observed quality deltas on your eval set.
3) Prompt set (v1) and evaluation harness + links to the results.
4) A staging plan and mutual action plan for a 2-week eval run.

Attachments included: prompt-set-v1.txt (sample prompts), preliminary benchmark CSV (placeholder). I'll follow up with Neha and Vivek to get the AWQ/GPTQ measurements on your eval set.

Next steps:
- Marissa to share recommended models + trade-study (today).
- FinWave to confirm the evaluation subset (Priya) and the staging window.
- Tech sync with Neha/Vivek for ops details (Tues/Wed).

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quantization tradeoffs and model-fit — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- On latency: the p95 <300ms target is strict during business hours; outside peak we can tolerate higher p95. Can you call out expected p95s for AWQ vs GPTQ at the candidate model sizes?
- Quality: when you say "<=5% regression" are you measuring top-1 answer accuracy or a human-rated correctness score? We will share our baseline metric but want to make sure comparisons are apples-to-apples.

Also: Priya asked whether the AWQ approach has any known failure modes with our safety prompts (we use a lot of negative-sample filters). Any heads-up there would be great.

If you can loop in your engineering contacts who will run the trade study, that'd be ideal. We can slot a 30-min technical sync Wed afternoon.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Engineering | FinWave
alex.johnson@finwave.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quantization tradeoffs and model-fit — please run AWQ/GPTQ comparisons

Team — forwarding the FinWave thread. Key asks:
- Provide AWQ and GPTQ quantization trade-study on FinWave eval set (attached). Include FP8 where possible.
- Produce measured metrics: token throughput (tokens/s and effective rps for their avg prompt length), memory footprint, and quality deltas vs baseline (please use both automated top-1 accuracy and a small human-rated sample for edge cases).
- Call out any known failure modes (safety prompt interactions, hallucination spikes, tokenization edge cases).

Context: FinWave target p95 <300ms, throughput up to 500 rps during scale windows. They care about <=5% quality regression. Prior notes: smaller AWQ profiles can give large throughput wins but occasionally increase distortion on certain token distributions (we saw this on finance ticker names previously).

Attachments: redwood-awsq-vs-gptq-summary.pdf (tech notes), finwave-benchmark-results.csv (sample harness output), prompt-set-v1.txt. Also linked a gist with earlier AWQ/GPTQ runs: https://gist.github.com/redwood-inference/awq-gptq-results

Request: Can you run the study on our NGC-8 cluster using the same model family candidates I recommended in today's doc and share a 1-page recommendation + the CSV by EOD Thu (18 Feb)? Prioritize p95 latency and top-1 accuracy. If FP8 yields measurable quality wins at similar cost, highlight that.

Thanks — loop back if you need additional infra requests.

Best,
Marissa
